docs.title: Rugby7 Referee Physical Fatigue Analyzer
docs.text:
Scientific software developed by SportsLabResearch for analysing external load, internal load and physical fatigue in Rugby Sevens referees.

The application imports match files, calculates locomotor and cardiovascular indicators, compares matches chronologically and generates reproducible Word, Excel and graphical reports.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Individual, multiple-referee and full-batch analysis.
  • Identified analysis preserving names, photographs and original filenames.
  • Private coded analysis using identifiers such as REF001, REF002 and REF003.
  • Automatic loading of .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm and .csv match files.
  • External-load analysis: total distance, relative distance, mean and maximum speed, speed zones and high-speed distance.
  • Internal-load analysis: mean and maximum heart rate.
  • Mechanical-load analysis: mean, total and relative AcelT.
  • Chronological trend analysis across matches.
  • Normalised load heatmaps.
  • Automated practical reports in Word and summary workbooks in Excel.
  • Anonymised outputs suitable for public repositories and Zenodo releases.

docs.title: Scientific workflow
docs.text:
1. Place each referee's files inside data/input/<referee>/.
  2. Run python main.py.
  3. Select identified or private coded analysis.
  4. Select one, several or all referees.
  5. Select one, several or all matches.
  6. Review the generated files inside data/output/.

docs.title: Current version
docs.text:
v0.1.0-alpha

The software is under active development. Validate the generated results before using them in research, publication or operational decision-making.

docs.title: Identified analysis
docs.text: This mode keeps real folder names and may include photographs and profile details in reports. It is intended for authorised local use.

docs.title: Private coded analysis
docs.text:
This mode replaces displayed referee identities with deterministic session codes:

REF001
REF002
REF003

Match names are also presented generically as Partido 01, Partido 02, etc. This reduces accidental disclosure through console output and generated filenames.

Pseudonymisation is not anonymisation

Codes can still be linked back to identities if the folder ordering, source files, photographs or external mapping tables are retained. Before public deposition, inspect every generated file and remove any residual identifiers.

docs.title: Recommended release workflow
docs.text:
graph TD
  A[Identified source data] --> B[Local analysis]
  B --> C[Private coded analysis]
  C --> D[Manual disclosure review]
  D --> E[Public dataset / Zenodo release]
  A -. never publish directly .-> X[Restricted storage]

docs.title: Module reference
docs.text: This page documents the stable entry points visible in the current alpha codebase.

docs.title: Command-line orchestration
docs.text:
from main import parsear_seleccion, obtener_codigo_arbitro

parsear_seleccion("1,3-5", total=6)
# [1, 3, 4, 5]

obtener_codigo_arbitro(7)
# "REF007"

docs.title: Input detection
docs.text:
from src.connectors.input_detector import detectar_arbitros

folders = detectar_arbitros()

docs.title: File loading
docs.text:
from src.connectors.excel_loader import (
    cargar_archivo_partido,
    cargar_varios_partidos,
)

result = cargar_archivo_partido("data/input/Referee/Partido_01.xlsx")
print(result["filas"], result["columnas"], result["hoja"])

The returned dictionary contains ruta, archivo, hoja, filas, columnas, nombres_columnas and the cleaned pandas DataFrame in datos.

docs.title: Analysis entry point
docs.text:
from src.analyzers.fatigue_analyzer import procesar_arbitro_seleccionado

procesar_arbitro_seleccionado(
    codigo="REF001",
    carpeta_arbitro="data/input/Referee",
    archivos_partidos=["data/input/Referee/Partido_01.xlsx"],
    modo_privado=True,
    idioma="es",
)

Warning

Internal functions in fatigue_analyzer.py may change during the alpha phase. Prefer the command-line interface or the high-level processing entry point.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
  CLI[main.py<br/>Interactive CLI] --> DET[src/connectors<br/>Detection and loading]
  DET --> ANA[src/analyzers<br/>Cleaning, metrics, figures, reports]
  ANA --> OUT[data/output]
  CFG[src/config<br/>Application metadata] --> CLI

docs.title: main.py
docs.text: Controls menus, mode selection, referee and match selection, and dispatches each analysis to procesar_arbitro_seleccionado.

docs.title: src/connectors/input_detector.py
docs.text: Discovers referee directories under data/input and returns them in case-insensitive alphabetical order.

docs.title: src/connectors/file_detector.py
docs.text: Classifies files inside a referee folder and provides the match-file list to the interface.

docs.title: src/connectors/excel_loader.py
docs.text: Loads supported Excel and CSV files, selects the first non-empty worksheet and returns cleaned data plus audit metadata.

docs.title: src/analyzers/fatigue_analyzer.py
docs.text: Contains metric computation, profile handling, graph generation, heatmaps, Word formatting, translation helpers and end-to-end referee processing.

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: The anonymization and reports packages provide clear locations for future separation of privacy and reporting logic from the main analyzer module.

  • Excel audit output;

docs.text:

  • stronger separation of analysis and report generation;

docs.text:
1. Create a focused branch.
  2. Add or update tests for selection parsing, file detection and metric calculations.
  3. Avoid committing identified participant data.
  4. Run the application with synthetic or authorised sample data.
  5. Build the documentation strictly.

docs.title: Documentation style
docs.text:
• Use concise scientific language.
  • State units explicitly.
  • Separate implemented behaviour from planned features.
  • Do not publish personal information in examples or screenshots.

docs.title: Folder rules
docs.text:
Each referee must have a dedicated subfolder within data/input. Auxiliary files may include a profile spreadsheet, a photograph and one or more match files.

data/input/
├── Referee_A/
│   ├── Partido_01.xlsx
│   ├── Partido_02.csv
│   ├── datos_Arbitro.xlsx
│   └── photo.png
└── Datos_arbitros.xlsx     # optional global profile table

docs.title: Workbook selection
docs.text: For Excel files, the loader scans the workbook and uses the first worksheet containing non-empty data. Entirely empty rows and columns are removed, column labels are stripped, and the index is reset.

docs.title: Recommended quality checks
docs.text:
• Keep one observation per row.
  • Preserve units consistently across all matches.
  • Avoid merged cells inside analytical tables.
  • Use stable column names between files.
  • Check heart-rate values and missing periods before running the analysis.
  • Keep personal identifiers out of files intended for public release.

Tip

File names may contain match numbers. The analyzer extracts numeric order where possible so that match progression is interpreted consistently.

docs.title: Source code
docs.text: Use GitHub releases for immutable software versions. Each release should contain the source archive automatically produced by GitHub.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation workflow publishes the main branch to GitHub Pages. A local static copy can be built with:

mkdocs build --strict

The generated site is written to site/.

docs.title: Research artefacts
docs.text: Use Zenodo for DOI-backed software releases and approved public datasets. Keep sensitive or identifiable source data outside public deposits.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The analyzer is a Python command-line application. It reads tracking and physiological match files, derives a consistent set of external- and internal-load indicators, compares matches chronologically and creates practical reports.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer
  • Match data in Excel or CSV format
  • One folder per referee under data/input
  • Write access to data/output

docs.title: Interpreting results
docs.text: The analyzer describes change across the selected match sequence. Results should be interpreted as a multidimensional profile rather than as a single fatigue score.

docs.title: Practical reading order
docs.text:
1. Confirm that all selected matches were loaded correctly.
  2. Inspect match duration and data completeness.
  3. Compare absolute volume with relative intensity.
  4. Review external and internal load together.
  5. Check whether trends are consistent across multiple indicators.
  6. Consider contextual factors such as match role, stoppages, temperature and tournament schedule.

docs.title: Direction of change
docs.text:
A lower value is not automatically worse or better. For example, reduced metres per minute could reflect fatigue, but it could also reflect match structure. Heart-rate responses can be influenced by heat, hydration, stress and sensor quality.

Scientific interpretation

The software supports descriptive and practical analysis. Causal claims require an appropriate study design, validated thresholds and statistical modelling beyond automated report generation.

docs.title: Processing sequence
docs.text:
graph TD
  A[Detect referee folders] --> B[Detect match files]
  B --> C[Read workbook or CSV]
  C --> D[Clean empty rows and columns]
  D --> E[Normalise column names]
  E --> F[Validate required variables]
  F --> G[Estimate duration and metrics]
  G --> H[Split or compare match segments]
  H --> I[Calculate changes and status]
  I --> J[Generate tables, figures and report]

docs.title: Descriptive design
docs.text: The current implementation computes match summaries and percentage changes relative to a reference point in the selected series. It also creates narrative interpretations and status categories to support applied review.

docs.title: Data cleaning
docs.text: Heart-rate processing excludes physiologically implausible values below 40 bpm or above 230 bpm. Excel reading searches for a usable worksheet, while CSV reading attempts automatic separator detection and common encodings.

docs.title: Transparency
docs.text: The source code remains the definitive specification. Thresholds, column mappings and report wording should be reviewed before each scientific release because the project is currently an alpha version.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The analyzer combines external-load, internal-load and mechanical-load indicators.

Metric Typical unit Interpretation Match duration min Estimated active observation duration Total distance m Accumulated locomotor volume Metres per minute m/min Relative running intensity High-speed distance/activity m or relative value Exposure to demanding locomotor actions Mean heart rate bpm Average internal cardiovascular response Maximum heart rate bpm Peak recorded cardiovascular response Mean AcelT a.u. Mean instantaneous mechanical load Total AcelT a.u. Accumulated mechanical volume Relative AcelT AcelT/min Mechanical intensity normalised by duration

docs.title: Why combine metrics?
docs.text: A referee may maintain total volume while relative intensity falls, or show stable external load with a higher cardiovascular response. Examining several indicators reduces the risk of interpreting one noisy signal as fatigue.

docs.title: Units and comparability
docs.text: Only compare files when variables and units are equivalent. Vendor exports can use different labels, sampling frequencies or definitions even when the visible metric name is similar.

docs.title: Outputs and reports
docs.text: The analysis generates complementary outputs for audit, interpretation and reporting.

docs.title: Excel summary
docs.text: *_resumen_fatiga.xlsx contains match-level derived indicators and enables independent checking or downstream statistical analysis.

docs.title: Trend figures
docs.text:
The standard figure set covers:

  1. metres per minute;
  2. high-speed activity;
  3. mean heart rate;
  4. relative accelerometry load;
  5. a normalised load heatmap.

docs.title: Heatmap audit workbook
docs.text: *_heatmap_auditoria.xlsx preserves the values used to generate the heatmap, improving traceability between visual output and tabular data.

docs.title: Practical Word report
docs.text: The Word report can include referee profile information, competition branding, figures, comments, match comparisons, a traffic-light summary and a glossary. Reports are produced in landscape orientation to accommodate wide scientific tables.

docs.title: Privacy and anonymisation
docs.text: The repository supports a privacy-oriented coded workflow, but safe research sharing still requires governance and manual review.

docs.title: Personal data that may appear
docs.text:
• names and folder names;
  • photographs;
  • profile spreadsheets;
  • document metadata;
  • original filenames;
  • free-text fields;
  • dates or event details that enable re-identification.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Run private coded mode.
  • [ ] Remove photographs and real-name profile files.
  • [ ] Inspect Word document properties and embedded media.
  • [ ] Inspect Excel hidden sheets, comments and metadata.
  • [ ] Confirm that file paths are not exposed.
  • [ ] Review small-cell and linkage risks.
  • [ ] Keep the identity-code key in restricted storage.
  • [ ] Confirm consent, ethics and data-sharing permissions.

Warning

The software cannot guarantee GDPR compliance or irreversible anonymisation. Compliance depends on the full data lifecycle, legal basis, institutional controls and disclosure risk.

docs.text: Selections are parsed by the command-line interface using a compact syntax.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1        # first referee or match
1,3,5    # selected items
1-4      # range
4-2      # interpreted as 2-4

Invalid tokens are ignored. If no valid index remains, the analysis is not launched.

docs.title: Batch strategies
docs.text:
• One referee: useful for quality control and iterative inspection.
  • Several referees: useful when a known subset should be processed.
  • All referees: useful for reproducible batch generation after source validation.

docs.title: No referees are detected
docs.text:
Confirm that folders exist directly below:

data/input/

The detector ignores files at this level and only returns subdirectories.

docs.title: No matches are listed
docs.text: Check that the referee folder contains supported .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .csv files and that auxiliary profile files are not being mistaken for match files.

docs.title: Excel file has no usable data
docs.text: The loader checks every worksheet and raises an error when all sheets are empty after removing blank rows. Open the workbook and confirm that the table contains actual values.

docs.title: CSV encoding error
docs.text: UTF-8 is attempted first, followed by Latin-1. Convert unusual encodings to UTF-8 when possible.

docs.title: PowerShell cannot activate the environment
docs.text: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass

docs.title: Documentation deployment fails
docs.text:
Run locally:

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs build --strict

Fix any missing navigation pages or invalid YAML before pushing again.

docs.title: Identified analysis
docs.text: This mode keeps the original referee name, photograph, folder name and filenames. Use it only in an authorised local research environment because the generated reports may contain personal data.

docs.title: Private coded analysis
docs.text: This mode assigns sequential identifiers such as REF001, REF002 and REF003. It also displays generic match labels rather than original filenames. Use this mode when preparing reproducible examples, public documentation or Zenodo deposits.

docs.title: Input detection
docs.text:
The application scans data/input and treats every subfolder as a referee. Match files are detected within each referee folder and sorted before selection.

For Excel files, the loader examines all worksheets and uses the first sheet containing data. For CSV files, it automatically attempts separator detection and supports UTF-8 and Latin-1 encoding.

docs.title: External load
docs.text:
Indicator Unit Interpretation Duration min Estimated effective duration of the match file. Total distance m Overall locomotor volume. Relative distance m/min Distance normalised by duration. Mean speed km/h Average movement speed. Maximum speed km/h Peak locomotor demand. High-speed distance m Distance accumulated at 15 km/h or above. Speed zones %, min, m Distribution in Z1–Z5 intensity bands.

The implemented speed zones are:

  • Z1: 0–6 km/h
  • Z2: 6–12 km/h
  • Z3: 12–15 km/h
  • Z4: 15–18 km/h
  • Z5: above 18 km/h

docs.title: Internal load
docs.text:
Indicator Unit Interpretation Mean heart rate bpm Average cardiovascular response. Maximum heart rate bpm Peak cardiovascular response.

Heart-rate values outside the physiologically plausible interval used by the analyser are excluded before summaries are calculated.

docs.title: Mechanical load
docs.text: Indicator Unit Interpretation Mean AcelT a.u. Mean instantaneous mechanical load. Total AcelT a.u. Accumulated mechanical volume. Relative AcelT AcelT/min Mechanical intensity normalised by duration.

docs.title: Excel summary
docs.text: The summary workbook consolidates match-level results and supports later statistical analysis, auditing and reproducibility checks.

docs.title: Word report
docs.text: The practical report includes referee information when available, descriptive tables, chronological figures, interpretation text and a load heatmap. Reports are created in Spanish by the current application entry point.

docs.title: Interpreting trends
docs.text:
The figures show match order on the horizontal axis and the selected indicator on the vertical axis. A decrease over consecutive matches may be compatible with accumulated fatigue, but interpretation must consider match duration, role, environmental conditions, recovery, measurement quality and tactical context.

The software generates descriptive evidence; it does not independently establish a clinical diagnosis or causal conclusion.

docs.title: Data protection
docs.text: Do not publish identified input folders or identified reports without an appropriate lawful basis, research approval and participant consent. For open repositories, use private coded mode and inspect every generated file before release.

docs.title: No referees are detected
docs.text: Confirm that referee folders are directly inside data/input.

docs.title: No matches are detected
docs.text: Confirm that files use one of the supported extensions and are located inside the selected referee folder.

docs.title: An Excel file cannot be loaded
docs.text: Open it manually and verify that at least one worksheet contains a non-empty table with a header row.

docs.title: A report omits a metric
docs.text: Verify that the input column name can be recognised and that the column contains numeric data. Different GNSS or tracking exports may require column-name adaptation in the analyser.

docs.title: Zenodo releases
docs.text: Zenodo can archive tagged GitHub releases and assign a persistent DOI.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Zenodo with the authorised organisation account.
  2. Open the GitHub integration settings.
  3. Enable SportsLabResearch-Rugby7-Referee-Physical-Fatigue-Analyzer.
  4. Confirm that .zenodo.json and CITATION.cff contain the correct creators and metadata.

docs.title: Create an archived version
docs.text:
git tag -a v0.1.0-alpha -m "v0.1.0-alpha"
git push origin v0.1.0-alpha

Then create a GitHub Release from that tag. Zenodo should ingest the release and mint a version DOI.

docs.title: After deposition
docs.text:
• Add the DOI badge to README.md and docs/index.md.
  • Replace the citation template with the final Zenodo citation.
  • Use the concept DOI for the project as a whole and the version DOI when exact reproducibility matters.
